# partner_generate playbook

partner_generate runs partner-API providers (Grok/xAI, Gemini/Nano Banana, BFL/Flux, OpenAI, Ideogram, ByteDance Seedream/Seedance, Kling, ElevenLabs, ...) through Comfy Cloud. Two execution paths, chosen automatically — you never select one:

- **Workflow-persist path** (models marked "persisted" below): a real Comfy Cloud workflow run on a GPU pod. Async — returns `{prompt_id, status: "submitted"}`; poll `get_job_status`, then `get_output`. The output lands in the user's asset library with a reopenable graph embedded.
- **Direct-dispatch fallback** (non-persistable models, and the media shapes the persist node has no input for): synchronous proxy call returning `structuredContent.results[]` of `{url, mime?, suggested_save_path, download_command}`. Not saved to the library. Most reference-image EDITS on the persisted models take the workflow-persist path above instead — your caller media is uploaded into the user's own Comfy input storage and wired into the node through a LoadImage; a shape the node cannot express (an OpenAI `mask`, an Ideogram style reference, more images than the selected tier has slots) is what falls back here.

## Registered models

The registry currently holds **25 slugs** (17 image, 7 video, 1 audio) across 12 providers: bfl (8), vertexai (3), byteplus (2), ideogram (2), kling (2), xai (2), elevenlabs (1), ltx (1), minimax (1), openai (1), qwen (1), veo (1). Every registered slug is dispatchable by partner_generate today, so that count IS the authoritative total for partner_generate: a complete enumeration of its models lists exactly these and stops.

Modalities partner_generate does NOT serve today: **music, svg, 3d** — a call with one of those `type`s is rejected pre-spend with a "does not serve type" error, so generate them with `run_template` instead (see the SVG / 3D / music section below).

To enumerate the registered models (a "which models can partner_generate run?" ask), derive the slug list from `search_models(source: "partner", limit: 100)` — one page holds the whole registry (each entry flagged `source: "partner"`, `type` = the modality), and check that its `metadata.returned` equals its `metadata.total`, which should in turn equal the total above; `total` counts matches BEFORE paging and the size budget, so a short `data` array beside a matching `total` means the page is partial — page on with `offset` until you have them all. A count ABOVE the total above means something extra matched the filter (on Comfy Cloud an imported model of your own can declare `source: "partner"` in its metadata); the catalog below is the authoritative registry, so reconcile against it and only cite a slug that appears there. Then group the returned slugs by provider and modality and cite that payload as your source; the catalog also carries the per-model params and routing detail. A text query like `search_models(q: "seedance")` returns a slug too, and `search_nodes(category: "partner/")` finds the underlying API nodes.

### image (17)

- `bfl/flux-pro-1.1-ultra` (persisted to the asset library): Generates an image from text with optional reference image and aspect ratios from 1:4 to 4:1 (Flux Pro 1.1 Ultra).
- `bfl/flux-kontext-pro` (persisted to the asset library): Edits an image from a prompt with aspect ratios from 1:4 to 4:1 (Flux.1 Kontext Pro).
- `bfl/flux-kontext-max` (persisted to the asset library): Edits an image from a prompt with premium quality (Flux.1 Kontext Max).
- `bfl/flux-pro-expand` (persisted to the asset library): Outpaints an image with per-side pixel expansion (Flux Pro Expand). Async: returns a `prompt_id` (poll `get_job_status` -> `get_output`) and saves to the library. Pass the source as `medias[{role:"image"}]` and the per-side pixel counts in `params` (`top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`).
- `bfl/flux-pro-fill` (persisted to the asset library): Inpaints an image using a mask region (Flux Pro Fill). Async: returns a `prompt_id` (poll `get_job_status` -> `get_output`) and saves to the library. Pass BOTH `medias[{role:"image"}]` and `medias[{role:"mask"}]` — the mask is a black/white image the same size as the source, and its white region is the area that gets repainted.
- `bfl/flux-2-pro` (persisted to the asset library): Generates an image from text with up to 9 reference images (Flux 2 Pro).
- `xai/grok-image-generate` (persisted to the asset library): Generates images from a text prompt using xAI Grok Imagine (synchronous). `params.model` selects the variant: grok-imagine-image-2.0 (newest — best editing and text rendering; used when none is named), grok-imagine-image, grok-imagine-image-quality, grok-imagine-image-pro. `params.quality` (low/medium) tunes the 2.0 variant.
- `vertexai/nano-banana-2` (persisted to the asset library): Generates or edits images via Google Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image). Pass `prompt` plus optional `image` / `images[]` (HTTPS URL or data URI) for reference-based generation or editing.
- `vertexai/nano-banana-2-lite` (persisted to the asset library): Generates or edits images via Google Nano Banana 2 Lite (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image). The cheap, high-throughput tier of Nano Banana 2 — ~1K output only. Good for drafts and iteration loops before spending on nano-banana-2 / nano-banana-pro. Pass `prompt` plus optional `image` / `images[]` (HTTPS URL or data URI) for reference-based generation or editing.
- `vertexai/nano-banana-pro` (persisted to the asset library): Generates or edits images via Google Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro Image). Higher-quality variant of Nano Banana 2; a MULTI-image reference call runs synchronously (instant URL) instead of saving to the library.
- `xai/grok-image-edit` (persisted to the asset library): Edits an image based on a text prompt using xAI Grok Imagine. Pass an HTTPS URL or data URI as `params.image`, or `params.images[]` (up to 10) for multi-reference composition — referring to them as <IMAGE_0>, <IMAGE_1>… in the prompt; the two are mutually exclusive. Runs as a Comfy Cloud job by default (returns a `prompt_id`, saved to the library) for 1-3 images; `params.mask`, `params.aspect_ratio`, `params.resolution`, `params.quality` or a 4th+ image switch it to the synchronous provider call, which returns an instant URL and skips the library. `params.model` selects the variant (grok-imagine-image default, grok-imagine-image-2.0 for the strongest editing/text rendering, grok-imagine-image-quality, grok-imagine-image-pro — that one takes a single image) and `params.quality` (low/medium/high) is forwarded to xAI.
- `bfl/flux-2-max` (persisted to the asset library): Generates an image from text with up to 9 reference images (Flux 2 Max).
- `openai/images-generations` (persisted to the asset library): Generates OR edits images using OpenAI (gpt-image-2 / gpt-image-1.5 / gpt-image-1). Specify `model` (via `params.model`) and `prompt` at minimum. Returns a `prompt_id` (poll `get_job_status` → `get_output`) and saves to the library. Pass `medias[{role:"image"}]` to EDIT an image — reference-image edits save to the library too; adding `{role:"mask"}` runs synchronously (instant URL) instead. Edits require `model` gpt-image-2 / gpt-image-1.5 / gpt-image-1.
- `ideogram/generate` (persisted to the asset library): Generates OR edits images using Ideogram. Text-to-image: pass `prompt` top-level; `params.image_request` is optional and only needed for provider-specific fields (`model`, `style_type`, `magic_prompt_option`, `negative_prompt`) — `style_type` / `negative_prompt` / a non-`V_3` `model` run on the synchronous direct path instead of the library run. Image edit: pass `medias[{role:"image"}]` (+ optional `mask` / `reference_image` / `character_image` / `character_mask`) to route to Ideogram V3 edit; `image` / `mask` / `character_image` edits save to the library, while `reference_image` (style refs), `character_mask`, `style_type` and `magic_prompt` run on the synchronous direct path.
- `ideogram/p-image` (persisted to the asset library): Generates images with Ideogram P-Image (Ideogram & Pruna), a fast text-to-image model with strong typography and photorealism, via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Pass `prompt` top-level; optional FLAT `params.quality` (VERY_LOW/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, default MEDIUM), `params.resolution` (1K/2K, default 1K), `params.aspect_ratio` (W:H, e.g. "16:9"), `params.prompt_upsampling` (AUTO/ON/OFF), `params.seed` (fixed default 42 — vary it across calls for different images). No `image_request` wrapper (that is the legacy `ideogram/generate` slug only — passing one here is rejected). Prefer quality HIGH + resolution 2K for crisp lettering.
- `qwen/qwen-image-3` (persisted to the asset library): Generates OR edits images with Qwen Image 3.0 (Alibaba) — strong on dense text, multilingual (English/Chinese) typography and infographic-style layouts. Text-to-image is async: it returns a `prompt_id` (poll `get_job_status` -> `get_output`) and saves to the library. Pass `prompt` top-level; the tier goes in `params.model` (`qwen-image-3.0-pro` default, cheaper `qwen-image-3.0`). Optional FLAT `params`: `negative_prompt`, `width`+`height` (pixels, supplied together; total area 512*512..2560*2560, aspect within 1:8..8:1 — omit both to let the model pick), `n` (1-6), `seed` (fixed default 42 — vary it for different images), `prompt_extend` (default true), `watermark` (default false). Pass 1-3 `medias[{role:"image"}]` / `{role:"reference_image"}` to EDIT or combine images instead — referring to them as @Image1/@Image2/@Image3 in the prompt. Edits are async too (they run the `QwenImageEditApi` node and save to the library); pass `width`+`height` on an edit only to force a size, otherwise the output matches the input.
- `byteplus/images-generations` (persisted to the asset library): Generates or edits images using ByteDance Seedream / SeedEdit. Specify `model` (e.g. `seedream-4-0-250828`) and `prompt`. URL or base64 reference images via `image`.

### video (7)

- `bfl/flux-3-video` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video (with synchronized audio) from text using BFL FLUX 3 Video via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt` and optional `aspect_ratio`/`duration`/`resolution`/`generate_audio`/`seed`. `duration` is a STRING of seconds ("5".."20") or "auto".
- `minimax/hailuo-03-t2v` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video from text using MiniMax Hailuo 03 (MiniMax H3) via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt` and optional `resolution` (768P/2K)/`aspect_ratio`/`duration` (4–15s)/`seed`/`watermark`.
- `byteplus/seedance-2.0-t2v` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video from text using ByteDance Seedance via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt` and optional `resolution` / `ratio` / `duration` / `seed`. For a cheaper, faster draft pass, set `model` to `Seedance 2.0 Mini` (~half the price of standard, ~2× faster than fast; 480p/720p only, 4–15s); `Seedance 2.0 Fast` (720p) and the default `Seedance 2.0` (up to 1080p) are the other tiers. For clips longer than 15s set `model` to `Seedance 2.5` (newest model, up to 30s, up to 1080p).
- `kling/kling-v3-t2v` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video from text using Kling V3 via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt` and optional `negative_prompt`/`resolution`/`aspect_ratio`/`duration`/`generate_audio`/`seed`. `duration` is an integer number of seconds (3–15), not a string.
- `kling/kling-3.0-turbo-t2v` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video from text using Kling 3.0 Turbo (speed-optimized, native audio) via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. `duration` is an integer number of seconds (3–15), not a string.
- `ltx/ltx-2-5-t2v` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video (with AI audio) from text using LTX-2.5 via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt`; the tier goes in `params.model` (default `LTX-2.5 (Fast)`, clips up to 20s and up to 3840x2160; `LTX-2.5 (Pro)` is 2/3/4/5/6/8/10s at up to 1920x1080). Optional `duration`/`resolution`/`fps` are STRINGS ("8", "1920x1080", "25"), plus `generate_audio`/`seed`. A Fast clip over 10s needs a 720p/1080p resolution at 24/25 fps. No `aspect_ratio` knob — `resolution` sets the orientation (e.g. `"1080x1920"` for portrait).
- `veo/veo-3-t2v` (persisted to the asset library): Generates video from text using Google Veo 3 via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt`; the tier goes in `params.model` (default `veo-3.1-generate`, the flagship). Optional `negative_prompt`/`aspect_ratio`/`resolution`/`duration_seconds` (4, 6 or 8)/`generate_audio`/`seed`. 4k renders on the `veo-3.1-generate` and `veo-3.1-fast-generate` tiers only.

### audio (1)

- `elevenlabs/sound-generation` (persisted to the asset library): Generates a sound effect from a text prompt using ElevenLabs (sound-generation) via a real Comfy Cloud workflow run. Output is saved to the asset library with a reopenable graph. Pass `prompt` and optional `duration` (0.5–30s) / `prompt_influence` (0–1) / `loop` / `output_format`.

## Non-obvious provider mappings

- **OpenAI images** (gpt-image-2 / gpt-image-1.5 / gpt-image-1): the registered `model` is `openai/images-generations` and the variant goes in `params.model` — NEVER pass `gpt-image-2` as the top-level `model` (bounces as "unknown model"). Text-to-image: `{ type: "image", model: "openai/images-generations", prompt: "…", params: { model: "gpt-image-2" } }`. Edits require `params.model` gpt-image-2 / gpt-image-1.5 / gpt-image-1; a reference-image edit persists to the library, while adding a `mask` routes the call to the synchronous direct path.
- **ByteDance Seedream images**: `model` is `byteplus/images-generations`; the actual model goes in `params.model` (e.g. `seedream-4-0-250828`).
- **Grok / xAI Imagine images**: the slugs stay `xai/grok-image-generate` and `xai/grok-image-edit`; the variant goes in `params.model` — `grok-imagine-image`, `grok-imagine-image-2.0`, `grok-imagine-image-quality`, `grok-imagine-image-pro` — and passing a variant id as the top-level `model` bounces. Name the variant explicitly rather than relying on a default: the two slugs resolve an omitted `params.model` differently — the generate slug persists through `GrokImageNode` and runs the variant that entry declares (`grok-imagine-image-2.0`, not the base tier), while the edit slug declares `grok-imagine-image` (matching xAI's own default for a call it forwards). Reach for `grok-imagine-image-2.0` on mask/region edits, multi-reference composition and text rendering. Edits take EITHER one source image (`medias: [{role: "image", …}]`) OR up to 10 references (`medias: [{role: "reference_image", …}, …]`, equivalently `params.images[]`) — the two are mutually exclusive, and with references you address them in the prompt as `<IMAGE_0>`, `<IMAGE_1>`… Billing passes through xAI's own reported per-request cost, so a multi-reference edit or a heavier variant is priced differently from a default one-image call. `params.quality` tunes the 2.0 variant — low/medium on the generate slug (what the ComfyUI node serves), low/medium/high on the edit slug, where supplying it routes the call to the synchronous provider call. Both slugs run as a Comfy Cloud job by default and save to the library; on the edit slug `params.mask`, `params.aspect_ratio`, `params.resolution`, `params.quality` or a 4th+ reference image switch it to the synchronous provider call, which returns an instant URL and skips the library (`grok-imagine-image-pro` takes a single image, so a 2nd one switches it too).
- **BFL Flux Pro fill / expand** (`bfl/flux-pro-fill`, `bfl/flux-pro-expand`): both run as a Comfy Cloud job and save to the library, so they return a `prompt_id` to poll. Expand outpaints — pass the source as `medias[{role:"image"}]` and the per-side pixel counts in `params` (`top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`, 0-2048). Fill inpaints — pass BOTH `medias[{role:"image"}]` and `medias[{role:"mask"}]`, where the mask is a black/white image the same size as the source and its WHITE region is the area that gets repainted.
- **BFL Flux 2** (`bfl/flux-2-pro`, `bfl/flux-2-max`): edit and reference inputs are `medias[{role:"image"}]` and/or `medias[{role:"reference_image"}]` — both collect into the node's `images[]`. The role is `reference_image`, never `reference` (that spelling bounces; the rejection names the accepted roles).
- **Ideogram**: text-to-image takes the canonical top-level `prompt`; `params.image_request` is optional and only needed for provider-specific fields (`model`, `style_type`, `magic_prompt_option`, `negative_prompt`) — a top-level `prompt` is threaded into `image_request.prompt` for you, and an explicit `image_request.prompt` wins on both execution paths (the library run fills its prompt from it too). `magic_prompt_option`/`seed`/`num_images` are honored on the default library run; `style_type`, `negative_prompt`, or a `model` other than `V_3` route the call to the synchronous direct path (instant URL, not saved to the library), where an unspecified `model` defaults to `V_2`. An image edit (`medias[{role:"image"}]` + optional `mask`/`reference_image`/`character_image`/`character_mask`) routes to Ideogram V3 edit; `image`/`mask`/`character_image` save to the library, while `reference_image` (style refs) and `character_mask` run on the synchronous direct path. `ideogram/p-image` is the P-Image (Ideogram & Pruna) text-to-image slug: it takes a top-level `prompt` and FLAT `params` (`quality` VERY_LOW/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, `resolution` 1K/2K, `prompt_upsampling` AUTO/ON/OFF) — only the legacy `ideogram/generate` slug uses `params.image_request`. For typography prefer `quality: "HIGH"` + `resolution: "2K"`.
- **Qwen Image 3.0** (Alibaba): the registered slug is `qwen/qwen-image-3` (the catalog row it is built from, `qwen/services-aigc-multimodal-generation-generation`, is a proxy path and is NOT callable as `model`); the variant goes in `params.model` — `qwen-image-3.0-pro` (default) or the cheaper `qwen-image-3.0`. Reach for it on dense text, multilingual (English/Chinese) typography and infographic-style layouts. Both routes persist to the library; an EDIT takes 1-3 images via `medias[{role:"image"}]` / `{role:"reference_image"}` (refer to them in the prompt as @Image1/@Image2/@Image3, in input order) and runs the `QwenImageEditApi` node, so it returns a `prompt_id` to poll just like the text-to-image half. Three is a hard cap on BOTH routes — a 4th image is refused pre-spend, not switched to another lane. `params.width`/`params.height` are pixel dimensions passed TOGETHER — total area 512*512 to 2560*2560 at any aspect ratio within 1:8..8:1 — and omitting both lets the model pick the resolution — on an EDIT, omitting both matches the input image's size. `params.seed` has a fixed default of 42, so vary it across calls for different images.
- **Seedance tiers**: `byteplus/seedance-2.0-t2v` picks a tier via `params.model` — `Seedance 2.0` (default, up to 1080p, 4–15s), `Seedance 2.0 Fast` (720p), `Seedance 2.0 Mini` (cheap/fast draft, 480p/720p only), `Seedance 2.5` (newest model, clips up to 30s, up to 1080p). 2.5 reaches 1080p too, so between those two the choice is length and price rather than resolution: pick `Seedance 2.5` for a clip longer than 15s. The Fast and Mini tiers are still 720p and 480p/720p respectively, so a 1080p request needs `Seedance 2.0` or `Seedance 2.5`. `Seedance 2.0` stays the default for an unpinned call.
- **LTX**: `ltx/ltx-2-5-t2v` is the registered text-to-video slug; the tier travels in `params.model` — `LTX-2.5 (Fast)` (default: clips up to 20s and resolutions up to 3840x2160, but a clip over 10s needs a 720p/1080p resolution at 24/25 fps) or `LTX-2.5 (Pro)` (2/3/4/5/6/8/10s at up to 1920x1080). `duration`/`resolution`/`fps` are STRINGS (`"8"`, `"1920x1080"`, `"25"`), not numbers, and `duration` is a SPARSE list — 2/3/4/5/6/8/10/12/14/16/18/20, so 7s or 15s bounces. There is no `aspect_ratio` knob — pick a portrait `resolution` (e.g. `"1080x1920"`) for a vertical clip; passing `aspect_ratio` anyway is refused with the resolution to use instead.
- **Google Veo**: `veo/veo-3-t2v` is the registered text-to-video slug; the tier travels in `params.model` (`veo-3.1-generate` default, `veo-3.1-fast-generate`, `veo-3.1-lite`, `veo-3.0-generate-001`, `veo-3.0-fast-generate-001`). 4k renders on the two `veo-3.1-*generate` tiers only.
- **Kling video**: `kling/kling-v3-t2v` / `kling/kling-3.0-turbo-t2v` take `duration` as an INTEGER of seconds, 3–15 (default 5) — pass `duration: 5`, never the quoted string `"5"` (the catalog's string enum is the raw partner API, not this tool's schema; a string bounces with "expected number, received string"). `resolution` is `"4k"` | `"1080p"` | `"720p"` (turbo: `"1080p"` | `"720p"`), `aspect_ratio` `"16:9"` | `"9:16"` | `"1:1"`, `generate_audio` boolean (ignored on turbo — 3.0 Turbo ALWAYS renders native audio); omitted knobs default (`1080p` / turbo `720p`, `16:9`, 5s, audio on).
- **Other named providers**: call partner_generate straight away with your best-guess slug — a slug that is not registered bounces back naming the closest registered ones, so the guess costs one call and a lookup round-trip costs the same. Take the workflow/template path once that bounce shows the provider has no slug; a slug belonging to a DIFFERENT provider is never the answer.

## medias[] — reference/edit inputs

Each item is EXACTLY ONE of: a Comfy-native reference `{role, prompt_id, output_index?}`, an uploaded input `{role, name}` (the `name` `upload_file` returned), or an external URL `{role, value}`.

- **Editing a Comfy Cloud output you already generated**: pass `medias: [{ role: "image", prompt_id: "<id from get_output/partner_generate>", output_index: 0 }]` — resolved server-side with the user's own creds; no public URL or upload_file round-trip needed.
- **`value` is for EXTERNAL images only** and MUST be a publicly fetchable https URL. A local file or a Comfy-uploaded `input` is NOT — its `/api/view` URL is auth-gated, so it 401s at the partner AND on the persist path, which server-fetches the same URL before uploading it into the user's own input storage. Pass a Comfy-uploaded input by `name` instead (next bullet).
- **Editing a LOCAL or freshly-uploaded image** (e.g. "make this photo a cyborg"): do NOT pass a `value` URL. `upload_file` the photo, then call `partner_generate` with `medias: [{ role: "image", name: "<name from upload_file>" }]` — the persist route wires that file into the edit node's LoadImage directly, saves the result to the library and returns a `prompt_id` to poll. If the persist route declines the request shape (the refusal says which part it could not wire), fall back to `submit_workflow` with a LoadImage node feeding the partner edit node's image input (e.g. `FluxKontextMaxImageNode.input_image`, `Flux2ImageNode.images`, the Grok edit node). Never base64-inline the image or route it through an external file host.

## SVG / 3D / music

No partner_generate persist path yet (a call returns a "does not serve type" error) — but they DO generate on Comfy Cloud via the TEMPLATE path. Switch to `run_template`, overriding the prompt: `api_recraft_v4_text_to_vector` (svg), `api_hunyuan3d_text_to_model` / `api_rodin3d_gen2_5_text_to_3d` (3d), `api_sonilo_t2m` / `audio_ace_step1_5_xl_turbo` (music); `search_templates({ q: <type> })` for more. Do NOT hand-build an OSS workflow for these.

## Handling results

- Workflow path: poll `get_job_status` → `get_output`; surface the `/api/s/<id>` shortlink VERBATIM — never resolve its redirect or paste the underlying `storage.googleapis.com` signed URL.
- Direct fallback: each result's `download_command` is a ready-to-run shell command (curl on darwin/linux, curl.exe on windows) — run it YOURSELF by default and execute it verbatim (the URL's query params carry the signature; do not reconstruct or re-quote it). Only if your own sandbox blocks egress (`403 Host not in allowlist` / connection / DNS error — an environment restriction, NOT an auth failure) hand the exact command to the user; never retry the identical command or re-authenticate.
